title: A ticket can go todo to done in one hop with no review and no evidence
description:
From the 2026-08-02 adversarial hardening run (hive-adversarial-improve, AC-fidelity chain). Probes A5 and P9. Two defects with one root cause: **`done` has no preconditions beyond the uat-only guard.**

**A5 — no state machine.** A `tdd`-tier ticket was created (`status: todo`) and closed straight to `done` in a single call. It was never `in_progress`, never `in_review`. Nothing anywhere requires that a review happened before a ticket closes. The `todo -> in_progress -> in_review -> done` sequence in CLAUDE.md is a described convention with no enforcement behind it.

**P9 — promises are not bound to receipts.** A `tdd` ticket whose acceptance criteria read:

```
1. A failing test is written first and its red run captured verbatim.
2. The feature is implemented and all tests pass.
3. npm run test:all is green.
```

closed to `done` with the comment body `"Done."` and no `linked_commits`, no reviewer comment, no evidence of any kind. Nothing mechanically relates an acceptance criterion to a proof that it was met — the entire binding is the reviewer's prose, and nothing checks that a reviewer ever ran.

**Why this matters more than it looks.** These are the two defects that make every other prose-level control optional rather than mandatory. The tier rubric, the red-run evidence discipline, the review-depth rubric, the AC-compliance check — all of them are things an agent is *told* to do, and A5/P9 show the mutation seam does not care whether any of them happened. This is not hypothetical: on 2026-08-02 TASK-175 closed to `done` with no independent reviewer at all, and the board is indistinguishable from a ticket that was properly reviewed.

**Fix direction (decide, do not assume).** Give `done` real preconditions at the mutation seam:
- A status-transition validity rule, so `done` is reachable only from a state that implies review occurred.
- An evidence requirement proportional to `verification_tier` — at minimum, a `tdd` or `tests-after` ticket should not close without a reviewer-authored comment and a non-empty `linked_commits`.

**This changes close semantics repo-wide and WILL break flows that currently work.** That is the point, but it means the migration is the hard part, not the check. Specifically: the repo's own `tasks/` contains ~180 already-`done` tickets, many of which never passed through `in_review` because the convention was not enforced when they closed. A naive rule makes the history retroactively invalid. Decide explicitly whether the rule applies only to new transitions, and prove the existing corpus still validates.

Note the related MEDIUM tracked separately in TASK-188: the loop-mode guards are composed by the MCP wrapper rather than living in the primitive, so a direct `closeTask` call (including the documented `Edit` fallback) skips them entirely. Any precondition added here should live where every caller gets it, not only the MCP path.

**Replayable fixture (protocol rule 2):** `ac-fidelity-probes.mjs` (P9) and `ac-fidelity-round2.mjs` (A5). Self-contained, temp-repo only. Port into `tests/`.
acceptance_criteria: Failing specs first replay probes A5 (a tdd ticket created as todo and closed straight to done in one call) and P9 (a tdd ticket whose ACs demand captured red-run evidence, closed with a four-word comment and no linked_commits), demonstrating both currently succeed. Capture the red-run output verbatim as the tests-first evidence.

Reaching status 'done' now requires a valid predecessor state that implies a review occurred — a todo -> done transition in one hop is rejected with a typed, named error rather than silently accepted.

Closing carries an evidence requirement proportional to verification_tier: at minimum a tdd or tests-after ticket cannot close without a reviewer-authored comment AND a non-empty linked_commits. Decide the exact requirement per tier and record the decision in the closing comment.

MIGRATION IS PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED: run the new rules against the repo's OWN tasks/ directory (~180 already-done tickets, many of which never passed through in_review). Demonstrate that no already-done ticket becomes retroactively invalid, or that the rule is explicitly scoped to new transitions only. State which, and show the check output.

The preconditions live where EVERY caller gets them, not only the MCP wrapper path — a direct closeTask/transitionStatus call must be subject to the same rules (see TASK-188 for the related guard-composition gap; coordinate rather than duplicate).

An escape hatch exists for legitimate exceptions (e.g. a ticket closed as won't-do, or a documented recovery path), and it is explicit and auditable rather than a silent bypass. If no escape hatch is warranted, say so and justify it.

The probe scripts are ported into the repo as permanent regression specs, each asserting the previously-MISSED input is now CAUGHT, per the hive-adversarial-improve protocol's replayable-fixture rule.

npm run test:all is green; no existing task-store, close-guard, mcp-server, drive-loop, or task-board spec regresses; dist bundles rebuilt and committed if bundled source changed, with dist-parity passing.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
**REQUEST-CHANGES** on FULL-depth review of `d97838b`. **1 HIGH / 2 MEDIUM / 3 LOW.** Ticket returns to `in_progress`.

## HIGH — the canonical procedure and the mutation seam now disagree on the DEFAULT path

`CLAUDE.md` Workflow steps 6-7; `skills/orchestrator-routing/SKILL.md:198-212, 1061-1085`.

`checkCloseEvidence` now requires, for `tdd`/`tests-after`, a **pre-existing `author: 'reviewer'` comment on disk** plus non-empty `linked_commits`, and `checkDonePredecessorState` requires the ticket to have reached `in_review`. Neither prerequisite appears in any document the Orchestrator *procedurally follows*:

- `CLAUDE.md` step 7 still instructs exactly one close action (`close_task` with an orchestrator summary comment). `git log` confirms it was last touched by `abc1049` (TASK-188); this commit did not update it.
- The routing skill was updated only in its **descriptive** guard list (1029-1059). Its **procedural** close section — *"On a clean review, call the `close_task` tool once"* (:1061) — and the worked `close_task` example (:1079-1084) are unchanged.

**This is not a rare path, it is the default one.** The migration data shows only **24 of 189** done tickets carry any reviewer comment, because established practice has been for the Orchestrator to write the closing comment as `author: 'orchestrator'` relaying the reviewer's findings. The reviewer made it concrete: **all five most recently closed tickets — TASK-196, 195, 194, 192, and TASK-188 itself, this control's own foundation — carry zero reviewer comments and would be rejected.**

**The compounding failure, which is the real finding:** both new error messages instruct exactly one remediation — `Pass exception: { reason }`, the bypass. With the honest path undocumented and the escape hatch advertised, the predictable steady state in unattended loop mode is **routine escape-hatch closes**, converting the control into audit noise. In the reviewer's words: *if the honest path is undocumented and the bypass is the advertised remedy, the speed bump gets driven around by the legitimate operator, not the adversary.*

CLAUDE.md's own rule — *"update it whenever a workflow decision changes"* — makes this in-scope for this ticket, not a follow-up.

**Fix:** update CLAUDE.md steps 6/7 and the skill's **procedural** close section and worked example (both parity copies byte-identical) to instruct the real sequence — transition to `in_review` when spawning the Reviewer; on PASS, `append_comment` with `author: 'reviewer'` recording the verdict; then `close_task` with `linked_commits`. And **reorder both error messages so the compliant remediation is named before the escape hatch.**

**Additionally — pin it, don't just fix it.** A prose fix here will drift again the next time the preconditions move; that is this session's most-repeated defect. Follow the TASK-196 precedent (`tests/uat-doc-example-lock.spec.js`): add a spec that **executes the documented close procedure against the real guards** and asserts it succeeds. If the code's preconditions change without the docs, the lock fails. Derive the steps from the doc rather than restating them.

## MEDIUM-1 — the escape hatch does not work at all for `uat-only`, and nothing says so

`src/task-store.js:1141` (checkUatGuard ordering) and the MCP tool descriptions. Empirically verified: `closeTask` with a valid `exception` on a `uat-only` ticket throws `UAT_GUARD_REQUIRED` before the exception is considered.

**Not bypassing `checkUatGuard` is the correct design** — the reviewer confirmed the hatch is not a skeleton key. But both tool descriptions advertise it for *"a legitimate exception (e.g. a won't-do closure)"* without qualification, and **AC6's own motivating example is a won't-do closure**. As shipped, a won't-do `uat-only` ticket has no legitimate close path short of fabricating an `Overall result: PASS` verdict.

**Fix:** document the `uat-only` exclusion in the tool descriptions and the SKILL block.

## MEDIUM-2 — discharged

The R3 checklist is present in the hand-off with all five items: unspecced path (escape hatch smoke-tested through the real MCP surface for accept and reject), red-green planted, dist rebuilt (exactly 2 bundles), parity SHA-confirmed, calibration n/a.

## LOW

1. `transitionStatus` appends a `[CLOSE-EXCEPTION]` comment on an **already-done** ticket even when both checks no-op'd — audit noise on idempotent re-closes. Guard the marker append on the status actually changing.
2. `resolveCloseException` accepts any `COMMENT_AUTHORS` value for `exception.author`, including `'reviewer'` and `'uat'`. The laundering paths are effectively dead (the `[CLOSE-EXCEPTION]` prefix defeats the verdict marker; `checkUatGuard` precedes the write), but restricting to non-privileged authors costs nothing.
3. Five new `makeTmpDir` disk-I/O tests sit in a top-level fast-tier file where CLAUDE.md's tier rule places them under `tests/e2e/`. Pre-existing convention in that file, continued rather than introduced. **Note only, no action.**

## Adjudications — both in the developer's favour

**Condition 2 departure: SOUND, accepted.** The reviewer independently tried to construct a real signal and failed: requiring a reviewer entry in the session bundle's `subagent_results` is also orchestrator-written, adding a fourth write but no identity anchor. `uat_delegated_to_orchestrator` is anchored in a *human's* out-of-band grant for a step loop mode legitimately skips; review is spawned unconditionally in every mode, so a reviewer-gate flag would be a self-set boolean in the same trust domain — friction, not a control. **And the control is described honestly** in the code, the commit, and SKILL.md's HONEST RESIDUAL block. It meets the standard TASK-188 set.

**AC2 probed:** `done` is reachable only from `in_review`, and a three-write fabrication (`todo → in_review`, plant reviewer comment, `close_task`) succeeds with zero actual review. That is exactly the residual the code discloses, so it is acceptable **as documented** — which is precisely why HIGH-1 matters.

## Verified good — do not redo

- **Migration recount reproduced exactly** by the reviewer's own script: 189 done, 24/189 with any reviewer comment, 160 tdd/tests-after done, 20/160 satisfying the new rule.
- **Behavioural probes all correct:** legacy done tickets stay fully mutable; idempotent re-close is a no-op; **`done → todo → close` is re-gated** (`E_INVALID_DONE_PREDECESSOR`), so idempotency cannot mint a fresh `done`; `in_progress → done` is rejected even with full evidence; the exception is **not** a skeleton key.
- **Non-vacuity proven behaviourally** — with both checks neutered to no-ops and the error classes still exported, A5 and P9 fail. The weak `instanceof … undefined` reds do not carry into the shipped specs.
- **dist correct:** only `mcp-server.cjs` and `task-board.cjs` contain `E_INVALID_DONE_PREDECESSOR`; the shrink from TASK-188's five is explained — that ticket also edited `src/close-guard.js`, which is embedded more widely.

## Gate (all green)

`test:since -- 0058398` 20 files / 263 tests ⬛ `npm test` 83 files / 1127 passed ⬛ named e2e 106 tests ⬛ close-guards + doc-locks 34 tests ⬛ **`test:all` 181 files / 2111 passed** ⬛ dist-parity byte-matched all 8 bundles ⬛ `check:calibration` clean.

comments.body:
**PASS — APPROVE.** FULL depth. 0 HIGH / 0 MEDIUM / 2 LOW.

Reviewed the fix round `c15cf37` (base `bfb342e`) against the prior round's HIGH: the canonical close procedure and the mutation seam disagreed on the default path.

**Both closing questions answered yes.**

*Can an Orchestrator follow the documented procedure end-to-end and close a `tdd` ticket?* Yes. CLAUDE.md steps 6/7, SKILL workflow steps 5/6, and the fenced CLOSE-PROCEDURE block all state the same three-call sequence, and the happy-path lock **executes that exact documented sequence** from a fresh `todo` fixture through the real guards to `status: done`. It ran green.

*Would the lock catch later code drift?* Yes, in **both** directions for the three gating preconditions. Tightening: a fourth precondition makes the happy path throw, because the test drives only the doc's extracted steps against the real primitives. Relaxing: the three mutation tests drive a corrupted sequence and assert the specific error class — if `DONE_PREDECESSOR_STATES` admits `in_progress`, mutation 1 fails; if the reviewer-comment requirement or its author check loosens, mutations 2/3 fail. Value-sensitivity confirmed: extraction parses `status` and `author` out of the doc's backtick calls, and each mutation self-checks `expect(mutated).not.toEqual(steps)`, so doc drift to a mutated value degenerates loudly rather than passing silently. Vacuity guards throw on missing markers and zero-step extraction.

**Old doc-lock meaning intact — not the TASK-188 pattern.** The preserved anchors still describe what the rewritten steps say; the new prose *adds* preconditions before the `close_task` instruction rather than rewriting around the anchors, and TASK-188's narrowed-scope sentence is retained verbatim in both copies.

**Error messages now teach the compliant path.** A reader hitting `E_CLOSE_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED` or `E_INVALID_DONE_PREDECESSOR` can execute the correct sequence from the message alone; the hatch is named last and framed as never a routine substitute. Both MCP tool descriptions match.

**LOW-1/LOW-2 verified no-regression.** `previousStatus` captured before mutation; a real bypass still appends exactly one marker with correct ordering; idempotent re-close appends none; `done → todo → close` re-gating unaffected. `EXCEPTION_AUTHORS` is a derived filter — `COMMENT_AUTHORS` is untouched, so `appendComment` still accepts `reviewer`/`uat` as the compliant path requires.

**Five dist bundles explained:** the new module-scope `EXCEPTION_AUTHORS` const is retained by esbuild in every bundle embedding any slice of `task-store.js`. The prior round shrank to two because it changed only guard-path code. dist-parity byte-matched all 8.

**LOW-1** — `tests/e2e/close-procedure-doc-lock.spec.js:125-131`: step 3's arguments are hardcoded in the harness rather than extracted from the doc's worked call, so drift *inside* that line (author edited to `reviewer`, `linked_commits` dropped) passes the lock. Fails loud at runtime with a typed error naming the remediation, and `linked_commits` is separately pinned by the P9 replays — hence LOW. Fix next time the file is touched: extract step 3's values the way steps 1-2 are extracted, and add a fourth mutation dropping `linked_commits`.

**LOW-2** — six more `makeTmpDir` specs in a top-level fast-tier file where the tier rule places them under `tests/e2e/`. Continuation of a pre-existing convention; fast tier still 2.7s. Note only.

**Gate:** `test:since -- bfb342e` 18 files / 202 tests ⬛ `npm test` 83 files / 1133 passed ⬛ named e2e 5 files / 92 tests ⬛ close-guards + doc-locks 40 tests ⬛ `test:all` **182 files / 2122 passed** ⬛ dist-parity all 8 bundles ⬛ `check:calibration` clean ⬛ both SKILL copies byte-identical.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
APPROVED and closed. Two commits: `d97838b` (close preconditions) and `c15cf37` (fix round aligning the canonical procedure and pinning it).

**This close is itself the feature's first live exercise.** TASK-187 is `tdd`, so closing it required the sequence its own code enforces: transition to `in_review` when spawning the Reviewer, record the verdict as a separate `author: 'reviewer'` comment, then `close_task` with `linked_commits`. That is the first close in this repo's history to follow the procedure — and it worked on the first attempt, which is the outcome the fix round existed to produce.

**Review depth: FULL** on both rounds. Rubric inputs: ~968 lines touching the guarded close path, the two canonical procedure documents, an escape hatch threaded through the MCP server and the board, and five dist bundles.

## AC3's decision, recorded here as the AC requires

**`tdd` and `tests-after` require a pre-existing reviewer-authored comment AND non-empty `linked_commits`. `uat-only` is excluded** — `checkUatGuard`'s content-checked verdict is already stronger than a presence check, and layering presence on top would add ceremony without adding signal.

## What the first round got right, and the one thing it missed

The mechanism was sound and was verified against the real corpus rather than asserted: 189 done tickets, only **24** carrying any reviewer comment, only **20 of 160** `tdd`/`tests-after` tickets satisfying the new rule. Those numbers are why the scoping matters — the checks gate **transitions into `done`**, never validity, so nothing on disk is re-gated. Verified behaviourally by the reviewer: legacy done tickets stay fully mutable, idempotent re-close is a no-op, **`done → todo → close` is re-gated** so idempotency cannot mint a fresh `done`, `in_progress → done` is rejected even with complete evidence, and the escape hatch is not a skeleton key — `checkUatGuard` fires first on `uat-only` tickets.

**What it missed was the procedure.** The code required three things; no document the Orchestrator *procedurally follows* mentioned any of them. CLAUDE.md step 7 still instructed a single `close_task` call, and the routing skill was updated only in its descriptive guard list — its procedural close section and worked example were untouched. The proof was blunt: **the five most recent closes, including TASK-188 which built this control's own foundation, would all have been rejected.**

**And the compounding half was the real finding.** Both new error messages instructed exactly one remedy — `exception: { reason }`. With the honest path undocumented and the bypass advertised, the steady state would have been routine escape-hatch closes, degrading the control into audit noise. As the reviewer put it: *if the honest path is undocumented and the bypass is the advertised remedy, the speed bump gets driven around by the legitimate operator, not the adversary.*

## The fix round, and why it is more than a doc edit

CLAUDE.md steps 6/7 and the skill's procedural section and worked example now state the real sequence, in byte-identical parity copies. Both error messages name the compliant path **first**, with the hatch last and framed as never a routine substitute.

The durable part is `tests/e2e/close-procedure-doc-lock.spec.js`, which follows the TASK-196 precedent: it **extracts the documented sequence from delimited markers in SKILL.md and drives the real `transitionStatus`/`appendComment`/`closeTask` with it.** Not a restatement of the grammar — an execution of the instructions.

The reviewer confirmed it closes the drift class in **both** directions. Tightening: a fourth precondition makes the happy path throw, since the test drives only the doc's extracted steps. Relaxing: three mutation tests drive a corrupted sequence and assert the specific error class, so loosening `DONE_PREDECESSOR_STATES` or the reviewer-comment requirement breaks them. Each mutation self-checks `expect(mutated).not.toEqual(steps)`, so drift in the doc toward a mutated value degenerates loudly rather than passing. Vacuity guards throw on a missing marker block and on a zero-step extraction.

## Condition 2 — the departure, adjudicated sound

TASK-188's reviewer specified pairing the presence check with a loop-mode write-gate on `author:'reviewer'`. The developer declined, reasoning that `uat_delegated_to_orchestrator` is anchored in a **human's** out-of-band grant for a step loop mode legitimately skips, whereas the Reviewer spawns unconditionally in every mode — so a reviewer-gate flag would be a self-set boolean in the same trust domain: friction, not a control.

This round's reviewer independently tried to construct a better signal and failed — requiring a reviewer entry in the session bundle's `subagent_results` is also orchestrator-written, adding a fourth write but no identity anchor. **Departure upheld.**

## What this control actually does — stated plainly

**It makes a fabricated close more expensive and more legible. It does not prevent one.** Three self-issued writes with no real review still reach `done`. What it buys is real: one-call closes are dead, every bypass leaves a greppable `[CLOSE-EXCEPTION]` marker, and a fabricated close now leaves three timestamped artifacts a human can audit.

The code, the commit, and SKILL.md's HONEST RESIDUAL block all claim exactly this and no more. There is no cryptographic identity available here — `developer`/`reviewer`/`researcher` subagents have no MCP tool access, so every call is the Orchestrator's session whatever author it writes — and the implementation declined to pretend otherwise. That accuracy is why it passed.

## LOW carried forward

1. `tests/e2e/close-procedure-doc-lock.spec.js:125-131` — step 3's arguments are hardcoded in the harness rather than extracted from the doc's worked call, so drift *inside* that line (author edited to `reviewer`, `linked_commits` dropped) passes the lock. Fails loud at runtime with a typed error naming the remediation, and `linked_commits` is separately pinned by the P9 replays. **Fix when the file is next touched:** extract step 3's values as steps 1-2 are extracted, and add a fourth mutation dropping `linked_commits`.
2. Six `makeTmpDir` specs in a top-level fast-tier file where the tier rule places them under `tests/e2e/`. Pre-existing convention; fast tier still 2.7s. Note only.

## Gate

`test:since -- bfb342e` 18 files / 202 tests ⬛ `npm test` 83 files / 1133 passed ⬛ named e2e 5 files / 92 tests ⬛ close-guards + doc-locks 40 tests ⬛ **`test:all` 182 files / 2122 passed** ⬛ dist-parity all 8 bundles ⬛ `check:calibration` clean.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
**CORRECTION to this ticket's closing comment — a claim in it is false and must not mislead a future reader.**

The closing comment states that this close was "itself the feature's first live exercise" and that following the three-step sequence "worked on the first attempt, which is the outcome the fix round existed to produce."

**That is wrong.** The close succeeded because the Orchestrator followed the newly-documented procedure, not because the guard enforced it. **The guard was not running.**

## Evidence

The live MCP server process holds a `dist/mcp-server.cjs` from before these guards landed, so `checkCloseEvidence` and `checkDonePredecessorState` were never in the executing code path this session. Two independent confirmations:

1. **TASK-200 was closed at 2026-08-04 09:58 with no pre-existing reviewer-authored comment** — 9.5 hours after this ticket's rule landed (`d97838b`, 2026-08-04 00:29). Replaying `hasCommentFromAuthor` against its pre-close comment set returns `false`, so the current rule *would* block that close. It succeeded anyway.
2. **TASK-201's sanitizer did not run** on a comment appended after `ffb1a53` rebuilt the bundle: three U+200D characters persisted into `tasks/TASK-201.json`, and TASK-201's own AC6 corpus sensor correctly flagged them. The shipped bundle contains `sanitizeCommentBody` (5 occurrences); the running server does not.

For completeness: TASK-193 (Aug 3, 22:56) and TASK-189 (Aug 3, 23:12) also closed without a pre-close reviewer comment, but both **predate** the rule and are therefore legitimate. TASK-200 is the only anomaly, and it is the decisive one.

## What remains true

The implementation, the specs, and the doc-lock are unaffected — they were verified against the real source by the reviewer, including a sandboxed plant proving the guards are behaviourally non-vacuous. `tests/e2e/close-procedure-doc-lock.spec.js` drives the real primitives directly, not through the MCP server, so its green result stands.

What is **not** established is any claim that the guard was observed enforcing itself end-to-end through the live tool surface. That verification has not happened yet and must not be inferred from this ticket's close.

## Why this matters beyond one wrong sentence

A guard added to the task-store primitive is **inert in any already-running MCP server until that server restarts**, and nothing signals the gap. The code is correct, the bundle is fresh, the tests are green — and the executing process is stale. This is exactly the shape this session has been fixing everywhere else: a control that looks active and is not.

Filed as its own ticket rather than left as a footnote here.
